office_does: A Snohomish County PUD commissioner sets policy for the customer-owned electric and water utility serving Snohomish County and Camano Island, including rates, power contracts, resource planning and reliability; in the general every PUD voter elects the District 1 seat.
race_blurb: Incumbent Sid Logan, commissioner since 2017, faces former Island County Commissioner Janet St Clair. Both promise low rates and reliable service; Logan runs on his rate and power-contract record, St Clair on doing more on climate and growing water and energy investments.

candidates.summary: Incumbent PUD commissioner since 2017 and Energy Northwest director, running on low rates, the revised BPA power contract, reliability and a 97% carbon-free supply.
highlights: Says five of his nine years had no general rate increase and expects none for 2027 [S1]
Advocated the revised BPA contract that he says removes exposure to extreme market prices [S1]
Endorsed by Rep. Rick Larsen, County Executive Dave Somers, Councilmember Nate Nehring and IBEW Local 77 [S1]

candidates.summary: Former two-term Island County commissioner and longtime nonprofit executive, running on low rates, grid resilience to climate and cyber threats, and expanded water and energy investment.
highlights: Eight years as Island County Commissioner and four terms as Board of Health chair [S1]
Promises low bills and reliable service and says the PUD must do more on climate and economic challenges [S1][S2]
Endorsed by Democratic legislators, Snohomish County Democrats and Washington Conservation Action [S1][S3]
